# Airframe

> Hangar's service catalog: Crossplane XRDs, compositions and the `airframe-application` Helm chart.
> One GitOps write path - nothing is applied with `kubectl`. Components (Redis, PostgreSQL, RabbitMQ)
> are entries in an environment's `components:` list; applications onboard through the bootstrap-tier
> XRDs (PythonApplication, NodeJSApplication, GoApplication, SpringBootApplication, InfraService).

## Start here

- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): what an agent may and may not touch, today - the human-and-agent-readable rules.
- [contract/airframe-contract.json](contract/airframe-contract.json): every chart field, every XRD's shape and summary, every component's real outputs (Secret/ConfigMap names and keys) - generated, never hand-edited. Query it with `tools/airframe-capabilities` instead of grepping source.
- [charts/airframe-application/values.schema.json](charts/airframe-application/values.schema.json): the single source of truth for the chart's values shape (descriptions, defaults, strictness). `values.yaml` is generated from it.

## Tools

- `tools/render-pipeline XR.yaml compositions/<x>/composition.yaml [--required FIX ...] [--observed OBS ...]`: render any composition through the real functions offline, no cluster or Docker (see its header).
- `tools/airframe-validate FILE...`: validate an environment values file against the strict schema, component output references, and dead-end convention rules. `--format json` for tooling.
- `tools/airframe-validate --xr FILE...`: validate XR requests (tenants/<app>/xr-requests/*.yaml) against the XRD schemas with unknown fields rejected (AF-XR-001..004, AF-SCHEMA-001/002): the pre-merge half of closing the silent-typo hole; the xr-requests Applications apply server-side for the other half.
- `tools/airframe-capabilities <components|component|targets|target|kinds|kind|verify|xrds|xrd|field|output> ...`: answer "what exists and what does it do" from the contract bundle alone.
- `tools/airframe-verify <kind> <namespace>/<name> [--context CTX] [--format json]`: run one XR's verify contract against a live cluster, read-only (conditions, Secret keys without values, resources, TCP/HTTP via kubectl port-forward, Dex token, read-only cloud CLI).
- `tools/gen_airframe_schema.py`, `tools/gen_component_outputs.py`, `tools/gen_contract.py`: regenerate the generated files above after editing their sources. Each has a `--check` mode for CI.

## Docs

- [docs/user/quickstart.md](docs/user/quickstart.md): onboard a new app end to end.
- [docs/user/quickstart-flight-api.md](docs/user/quickstart-flight-api.md), [docs/user/quickstart-broker.md](docs/user/quickstart-broker.md): worked component examples (RabbitMQ publish/consume).
- [docs/user/decommission-app.md](docs/user/decommission-app.md): tear down an app.
- [docs/user/cloud-targets.md](docs/user/cloud-targets.md): stand up (and tear down) the AWS Lambda, ECS or Azure Container Apps infrastructure a cloud deploy needs - `AwsLambdaTarget`, `AwsEcsTarget`, `AzureContainerAppTarget`.

- [docs/admin/governance.md](docs/admin/governance.md): governance and security policy - who owns which decision, the enforcement ladder (XRD schema, pre-merge checks, compositions, management policies, identity, write path), what is enforced today versus convention, and how a policy change ships.
- [docs/admin/api-versioning.md](docs/admin/api-versioning.md): what catalog.hangar.io/v1alpha1 promises, which schema changes are breaking, how a new version ships (no conversion webhook), name-length limits, defaultCompositionRef, attach-mode Usages.
- [docs/admin/cloud-credentials.md](docs/admin/cloud-credentials.md): the cloud identities behind the cloud targets - the Crossplane provider identity (`hangar-crossplane`) versus the Glidepath deployer (`glidepath-deployer`) in AWS and Azure: exact IAM policies and Azure roles, where each secret lives, who can read it, what each can and cannot do, rotation.

## Optional

- [xrds/](xrds/): every XRD's real OpenAPI schema, if the contract bundle's summary isn't enough. `xrds/<type>.meta.yaml` is a component's sidecar output contract, the source `gen_contract.py` reads.
- [compositions/](compositions/): what each XRD actually renders, if you need to know exactly which Kubernetes objects a component creates.
